[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/02/Julius_Erving_%E2%80%93_76ers_%281%29.jpeg/250px-Julius_Erving_%E2%80%93_76ers_%281%29.jpeg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Julius_Erving_%E2%80%93_76ers_(1).jpeg)

Erving in 1976

The Nets, [Nuggets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1976%E2%80%9377_Denver_Nuggets_season "1976–77 Denver Nuggets season"), [Indiana Pacers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1976%E2%80%9377_Indiana_Pacers_season "1976–77 Indiana Pacers season") and [San Antonio Spurs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1976%E2%80%9377_San_Antonio_Spurs_season "1976–77 San Antonio Spurs season") joined the NBA for the [1976–1977 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1976%E2%80%931977_NBA_season "1976–1977 NBA season"). With Erving and [Nate Archibald](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nate_Archibald "Nate Archibald") (acquired in a trade with [Kansas City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1976%E2%80%9377_Kansas_City_Kings_season "1976–77 Kansas City Kings season")), the Nets were poised to pick up right where they left off. However, the [New York Knicks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1976%E2%80%9377_New_York_Knicks_season "1976–77 New York Knicks season") upset the Nets' plans when they demanded that the Nets pay them $4.8 million for "invading" the Knicks' NBA territory. Coming on the heels of the fees the Nets had to pay for joining the NBA, owner [Roy Boe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roy_Boe "Roy Boe") reneged on a promise to raise Erving's salary. Erving refused to play under these conditions and held out in training camp.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr_Jay#cite_note-42)

After several teams such as the [Milwaukee Bucks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1976%E2%80%9377_Milwaukee_Bucks_season "1976–77 Milwaukee Bucks season"), [Los Angeles Lakers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1976%E2%80%9377_Los_Angeles_Lakers_season "1976–77 Los Angeles Lakers season") and [Philadelphia 76ers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1976%E2%80%9377_Philadelphia_76ers_season "1976–77 Philadelphia 76ers season") lobbied to obtain him, the Nets offered Erving's contract to the Knicks in return for waiving the indemnity, but the Knicks turned it down. This was considered one of the worst decisions in franchise history.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr_Jay#cite_note-43) The Sixers then decided to offer to buy Erving's contract for $3 million—roughly the same amount as the Nets' expansion fee—and Boe had little choice but to accept the deal.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr_Jay#cite_note-44) For all intents and purposes, the Nets traded their franchise player for a berth in the NBA. The Erving deal left the Nets in ruin; they promptly crashed to a 22–60 record, the worst in the league.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr_Jay#cite_note-45) Years later, Boe regretted having to trade Erving to join the NBA, saying, "The merger agreement killed the Nets as an NBA franchise."[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr_Jay#cite_note-46)

Erving requested the No. 32 jersey that he had worn in the ABA, but was informed that it was to be retired for [Billy Cunningham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billy_Cunningham "Billy Cunningham"). He then decided to wear No. 6 instead in honor of [Bill Russell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Russell "Bill Russell"), who had been one of his heroes growing up.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr_Jay#cite_note-47)[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr_Jay#cite_note-48) Erving quickly became the leader of his new club and led them to an exciting 50-win season. However, playing with other stars-such as former ABA standout [George McGinnis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_McGinnis "George McGinnis"), future NBA All-Star [Lloyd Free](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_B._Free "World B. Free") and aggressive [Doug Collins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doug_Collins_(basketball) "Doug Collins (basketball)") allowed him to focus on playing more team-oriented ball. Despite a smaller role, Erving stayed unselfish. The Sixers won the Atlantic Division and were the top drawing team in the NBA. They defeated the defending champions, the [Boston Celtics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1976%E2%80%9377_Boston_Celtics_season "1976–77 Boston Celtics season"), to win the Eastern Conference. Erving took them into the [NBA Finals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1977_NBA_Finals "1977 NBA Finals") against the [Portland Trail Blazers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1976%E2%80%9377_Portland_Trail_Blazers_season "1976–77 Portland Trail Blazers season") of [Bill Walton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Walton "Bill Walton"). After the Sixers took a 2–0 lead, however, the Blazers ran off four straight victories after the famous brawl between [Maurice Lucas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maurice_Lucas "Maurice Lucas") and [Darryl Dawkins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darryl_Dawkins "Darryl Dawkins") which ignited the Blazers' team.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr_Jay#cite_note-49)

[![Image 10](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/eb/JuliusErvingSlamDunk1981.jpg/250px-JuliusErvingSlamDunk1981.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:JuliusErvingSlamDunk1981.jpg)

Erving playing against the Atlanta Hawks in 1981

Erving enjoyed success off the court, becoming one of the first basketball players to endorse many products and to have a shoe marketed under his name. He also starred in the 1979 basketball comedy film, _[The Fish That Saved Pittsburgh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Fish\_That\_Saved\_Pittsburgh "The Fish That Saved Pittsburgh")_. In the following years, Erving coped with a team that was not yet playing at his level. It took a few years for the Sixers franchise to build around Erving. Eventually, coach [Billy Cunningham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billy_Cunningham "Billy Cunningham") and top-level players like [Maurice Cheeks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maurice_Cheeks "Maurice Cheeks"), [Andrew Toney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Toney "Andrew Toney"), and [Bobby Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bobby_Jones_(basketball,_born_1951) "Bobby Jones (basketball, born 1951)") were added to the mix and the franchise was very successful.

The Sixers were still eliminated twice in the [Eastern Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Conference_(NBA) "Eastern Conference (NBA)") Finals. In 1979, [Larry Bird](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Larry_Bird "Larry Bird") entered the league, reviving the [Boston Celtics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston_Celtics "Boston Celtics") and the storied [Celtics–76ers rivalry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celtics%E2%80%9376ers_rivalry "Celtics–76ers rivalry"); these two teams faced each other in the Eastern Conference Finals in 1980, 1981, 1982 and 1985. The Bird vs. Erving matchup became arguably the top personal rivalry in the sport (along with Bird vs. [Magic Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magic_Johnson "Magic Johnson")), inspiring the early [Electronic Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_Arts "Electronic Arts")[video game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Video_game "Video game")_[One on One: Dr. J vs. Larry Bird](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One\_on\_One:\_Dr.\_J\_vs.\_Larry\_Bird "One on One: Dr. J vs. Larry Bird")_. In 1980, the 76ers prevailed over the Celtics to advance to [the NBA Finals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1980_NBA_Finals "1980 NBA Finals") against the [Los Angeles Lakers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1979%E2%80%9380_Los_Angeles_Lakers_season "1979–80 Los Angeles Lakers season"). There, Erving executed the legendary "Baseline Move", a behind-the-board reverse layup. However, the Lakers won the series 4–2 with superb play from, among others, Magic Johnson. Erving also made the only three point shot in that NBA Finals series, which was the first time the three point line was introduced in the league.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr_Jay#cite_note-50)

Erving was again among the league's best players in the 1980–1981 and 1981–1982 seasons, although more disappointment came as the Sixers stumbled twice in the playoffs: in 1981, the [Celtics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1980%E2%80%9381_Boston_Celtics_season "1980–81 Boston Celtics season") eliminated them in seven games in the 1981 Eastern Finals after [Philadelphia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1981%E2%80%9382_Philadelphia_76ers_season "1981–82 Philadelphia 76ers season") had a 3–1 series lead, but lost both Game 5 and Game 6 by 2 points and the deciding Game 7 by 1; and in 1982, the Sixers managed to beat the defending champion Celtics in seven games in the 1982 Eastern Finals but lost the NBA Finals to the [Los Angeles Lakers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1981%E2%80%9382_Los_Angeles_Lakers_season "1981–82 Los Angeles Lakers season") in six games. Despite these defeats, Erving was named the NBA [MVP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_Most_Valuable_Player_Award "NBA Most Valuable Player Award") in 1981 and was again voted to the 1982 All-NBA First Team.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr_Jay#cite_note-51)

For the [1982–1983 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1982%E2%80%931983_NBA_season "1982–1983 NBA season"), the Sixers obtained the missing element to combat their weakness at their center position, [Moses Malone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moses_Malone "Moses Malone"). Armed with a highly regarded center-forward combination, the [Sixers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1982%E2%80%9383_Philadelphia_76ers_season "1982–83 Philadelphia 76ers season") dominated the whole season, prompting Malone to make the famous playoff prediction of "fo-fo-fo (four-four-four)" in anticipation of the 76ers sweeping the three rounds of the playoffs en route to an NBA title.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr_Jay#cite_note-52) In fact, the Sixers went four-five-four, losing one game to the [Milwaukee Bucks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1982%E2%80%9383_Milwaukee_Bucks_season "1982–83 Milwaukee Bucks season") in the conference finals, then sweeping the [Lakers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1982%E2%80%9383_Los_Angeles_Lakers_season "1982–83 Los Angeles Lakers season") to win the NBA title.

[![Image 11](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/9/9d/Erving_Lipofsky.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail_unscaled)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Erving_Lipofsky.jpg)

Erving during his final season in 1987

Erving maintained his all-star caliber of play into his twilight years, averaging 22.4, 20.0, 18.1 and 16.8 points per game in his final seasons.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr_Jay#cite_note-53) In 1986, he announced that he would retire after the season. That final season saw opposing teams pay tribute to Erving in the last game he would play in their arenas, including in cities such as Boston and Los Angeles, his perennial rivals in the playoffs.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr_Jay#cite_note-54) On April 17, 1987, against the [Indiana Pacers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indiana_Pacers "Indiana Pacers"), Erving scored a season-high 38 points in front of the Philadelphia crowd in his final home game to score his 30,000th combined point as an ABA/NBA player.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr_Jay#cite_note-55) He closed his career out with a loss to the [Milwaukee Bucks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milwaukee_Bucks "Milwaukee Bucks") in the first round.

### Retirement

Erving retired in 1987 at the age of 37. [Johnny Kerr](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnny_Kerr "Johnny Kerr") told ABA historian [Terry Pluto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terry_Pluto "Terry Pluto"): "A young Julius Erving was like Thomas Edison, he was always inventing something new every night." He is also one of the few players in modern basketball to have his number retired by two franchises: the Brooklyn Nets (formerly the New York Nets and New Jersey Nets) have retired his No. 32 jersey and the Philadelphia 76ers his No. 6 jersey. He was an excellent all around player who was also an underrated defender. In his ABA days, he would guard the best forward, whether small forward or power forward, for over 40 minutes a game and simultaneously be the best passer, ball handler and clutch scorer every night. Many of Erving's acrobatic highlight feats and clutch moments were unknown because of the ABA's scant television coverage. He is considered by many as the greatest dunker of all time.

In his ABA and NBA careers combined, he scored more than 30,000 points. In 1993, Erving was elected to the [Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naismith_Memorial_Basketball_Hall_of_Fame "Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame") and in 1996 he was inducted into the [NYC Basketball Hall of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NYC_Basketball_Hall_of_Fame "NYC Basketball Hall of Fame"). When he retired, Erving ranked in the top five in scoring (third), field goals made (third), field goals attempted (fifth) and steals (first). On the combined NBA/ABA scoring list, Erving ranked third with 30,026 points. As of 2022[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Julius_Erving&action=edit), Erving ranks eighth on the list, behind only [LeBron James](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LeBron_James "LeBron James"), [Kareem Abdul-Jabbar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kareem_Abdul-Jabbar "Kareem Abdul-Jabbar"), [Karl Malone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl_Malone "Karl Malone"), [Kobe Bryant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kobe_Bryant "Kobe Bryant"), [Michael Jordan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Jordan "Michael Jordan"), [Dirk Nowitzki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dirk_Nowitzki "Dirk Nowitzki") and [Wilt Chamberlain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilt_Chamberlain "Wilt Chamberlain").

### 1976 ABA Slam Dunk Contest

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Julius_Erving&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: 1976 ABA Slam Dunk Contest")]

[![Image 14](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6a/Philadelphia_Sports_Statues_10.jpg/250px-Philadelphia_Sports_Statues_10.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Philadelphia_Sports_Statues_10.jpg)

Erving statue in South Philadelphia unveiled in January 1989

In this memorable contest, Erving faced [George "The Iceman" Gervin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Gervin "George Gervin"), All-Star and former teammate [Larry "Special K" Kenon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Larry_Kenon "Larry Kenon"), MVP [Artis "The A-Train" Gilmore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artis_Gilmore "Artis Gilmore") and [David "The Skywalker" Thompson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Thompson_(basketball) "David Thompson (basketball)"). Erving started by dunking two balls in the hoop. Then, he performed a move that brought the slam dunk contest to the national consciousness. He ran to the opposite end of the court and back and dunked the basketball from the free throw line. Although dunking from the foul line had been done by other players ([Jim Pollard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Pollard "Jim Pollard") and [Wilt Chamberlain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilt_Chamberlain "Wilt Chamberlain") in the 1950s, for example), Erving introduced the dunk from the foul line to a wider audience, when he demonstrated the feat in the [1976 ABA All-Star Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1976_ABA_All-Star_Game "1976 ABA All-Star Game") Slam Dunk Contest.

### Dunk over Bill Walton

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Julius_Erving&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Dunk over Bill Walton")]

This event transpired during game 6 of the [1977 NBA Finals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1977_NBA_Finals "1977 NBA Finals"). After Portland scored a basket, Erving immediately ran the length of the court with the entire Blazers team defending him. He performed a crossover to blow by multiple defenders, seemingly gliding to the hoop with ease. With UCLA defensive legend [Bill Walton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Walton "Bill Walton") waiting in the post, Erving threw down a vicious slam dunk over Walton's outstretched arms. This dunk is considered by many to be one of the strongest dunks ever attempted,[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] considering he ran full court with all five defenders running with him. This move was one of the highlights of his arrival to a more television-exposed NBA.

### Baseline move

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Julius_Erving&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Baseline move")]

One of his most memorable plays occurred during the [1980 NBA Finals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1980_NBA_Finals "1980 NBA Finals"), when he executed a seemingly impossible finger-roll behind the backboard.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr_Jay#cite_note-56)[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr_Jay#cite_note-57) He drove past Lakers forward [Mark Landsberger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Landsberger "Mark Landsberger") on the right baseline and went in for a [layup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Layup "Layup"). Then 7′2″ center [Kareem Abdul-Jabbar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kareem_Abdul-Jabbar "Kareem Abdul-Jabbar") crossed his way, blocking the route to the basket and forcing him outwards. In mid-air, it was apparent that Erving would land behind the backboard. But somehow he managed to reach over and score on a right-handed layup despite the fact that his whole body, including his left shoulder, was already behind the hoop. This move, along with his free-throw line dunk, has become one of the signature events of his career. It was called by _Sports Illustrated_, "The, No Way, even for Dr. J, Flying Reverse Lay-up". Dr. J called it "just another move".

### "Rock the Baby" dunk over Michael Cooper

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Julius_Erving&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: \"Rock the Baby\" dunk over Michael Cooper")]

Another of Erving's most memorable plays came in the final moments of a regular-season game against the Los Angeles Lakers in 1983. After Sixers point guard [Maurice Cheeks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maurice_Cheeks "Maurice Cheeks") deflected a pass by Lakers forward [James Worthy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Worthy "James Worthy"), Erving picked up the ball and charged down the court's left side, with one defender to beat—the Lakers' top defender [Michael Cooper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Cooper "Michael Cooper"). As he came inside of the 3-point line, he cupped the ball into his wrist and forearm, rocking the ball back and forth before taking off for what Lakers radio broadcaster [Chick Hearn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chick_Hearn "Chick Hearn") best described as a "Rock the Baby" [slam dunk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slam_dunk "Slam dunk"): he slung the ball around behind his head and dunked over a ducking Cooper. This dunk is generally regarded as one of the greatest dunks of all time.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr_Jay#cite_note-58)

## Post-basketball career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Julius_Erving&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Post-basketball career")]

[![Image 15](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/27/Basketball_Legends.jpg/250px-Basketball_Legends.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Basketball_Legends.jpg)

Erving (top left) with other former NBA players visit the New York [NBA Store](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_Store "NBA Store") in January 2005

Erving earned his bachelor's degree in 1986 through the [University Without Walls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_Without_Walls "University Without Walls") at the [University of Massachusetts Amherst](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Massachusetts_Amherst "University of Massachusetts Amherst").[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr_Jay#cite_note-59)[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr_Jay#cite_note-60)[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr_Jay#cite_note-61) After his basketball career ended, he became a businessman, obtaining ownership of a [Coca-Cola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coca-Cola "Coca-Cola") bottling plant in [Philadelphia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia "Philadelphia") and doing work as a television analyst. In 1997, he joined the front office of the [Orlando Magic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic "Orlando Magic") as Vice President of RDV Sports and Executive Vice President.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr_Jay#cite_note-62)

Erving and former NFL running back [Joe Washington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Washington "Joe Washington") fielded a [NASCAR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASCAR "NASCAR")[Busch Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Busch_Series "Busch Series") team from 1998 to 2000,[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr_Jay#cite_note-63) becoming the first ever NASCAR racing team at any level owned completely by minorities. The team had secure sponsorship from [Dr Pepper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr_Pepper "Dr Pepper") for most of its existence. Erving, a racing fan himself, stated that his foray into NASCAR was an attempt to raise interest in NASCAR among African-Americans.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] He has also served on the [Board of Directors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Board_of_Directors "Board of Directors") of [Converse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converse_(company) "Converse (company)") (prior to their 2001 bankruptcy), [Darden Restaurants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darden_Restaurants "Darden Restaurants"), [Saks Incorporated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saks_Incorporated "Saks Incorporated") and [The Sports Authority](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Sports_Authority "The Sports Authority"). As of 2009, Erving was the owner of _The Celebrity Golf Club International_ outside of Atlanta, but the club was forced to file for bankruptcy soon after.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr_Jay#cite_note-64) He was ranked by [ESPN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ESPN "ESPN") as one of the greatest athletes of the 20th century.

In 1991 he performed the narration in a performance of Copland's [Lincoln Portrait](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lincoln_Portrait "Lincoln Portrait") with the [Philadelphia Orchestra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia_Orchestra "Philadelphia Orchestra") under [Riccardo Muti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riccardo_Muti "Riccardo Muti") in a concert to honor the 62nd birthday of the late [Martin Luther King Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_Luther_King_Jr. "Martin Luther King Jr.") The concert was broadcast and is available on [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube").

Erving made a cameo appearance in the 1993 movie _[Philadelphia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia\_(film) "Philadelphia (film)")_ starring [Tom Hanks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Hanks "Tom Hanks") and [Denzel Washington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denzel_Washington "Denzel Washington") and in the sitcom _[Hangin' with Mr. Cooper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hangin'\_with\_Mr.\_Cooper "Hangin' with Mr. Cooper")_ in 1995.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr_Jay#cite_note-65)[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr_Jay#cite_note-66) He appeared as The Minister in the [2012 remake of _Steel Magnolias_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steel_Magnolias_(2012_film) "Steel Magnolias (2012 film)") for Lifetime television.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr_Jay#cite_note-67) He also made a cameo appearance as himself in "[Lice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lice_(The_Office) "Lice (The Office)")", the tenth episode of the ninth season of the comedy series _[The Office](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Office\_(American\_TV\_series) "The Office (American TV series)")_ (2013).[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr_Jay#cite_note-tvequals-68) Erving appeared as himself in the 2022 movie [_Hustle_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hustle_(2022_film) "Hustle (2022 film)") starring Adam Sandler and [Juancho Hernangómez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juancho_Hernang%C3%B3mez "Juancho Hernangómez").

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Julius_Erving&action=edit&section=21 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Erving is a [Christian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christians "Christians"). He has spoken about his faith, saying: "After searching for the meaning of life for over ten years, I found the meaning in [Jesus Christ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jesus_Christ "Jesus Christ")."[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr_Jay#cite_note-91)

Erving is a second cousin of economist [Walter E. Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walter_E._Williams "Walter E. Williams").[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr_Jay#cite_note-92)

Erving was married to Turquoise Erving from 1972 until 2003. Together they had four children. In 2000, their 19-year-old son Cory went missing for 38 days, until he was found drowned after driving his vehicle into a pond.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr_Jay#cite_note-93)

[![Image 17: Erving standing next to the statue depicting his likeness at the UMass unveiling ceremony in Amherst, Mass., in September 2021.](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/00/Erving_standing_next_to_his_statue_at_UMass_unveiling_ceremony%2C_Sep_10_2021.jpg/250px-Erving_standing_next_to_his_statue_at_UMass_unveiling_ceremony%2C_Sep_10_2021.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Erving_standing_next_to_his_statue_at_UMass_unveiling_ceremony,_Sep_10_2021.jpg)

Erving standing next to the statue depicting his likeness at the UMass unveiling ceremony in Amherst, Mass., in September 2021.

In 1979, Erving began an affair with sportswriter Samantha Stevenson, resulting in the 1980 birth of [Alexandra Stevenson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexandra_Stevenson "Alexandra Stevenson"), who would become a professional tennis player. Although Erving's fatherhood of Alexandra Stevenson was known privately to the families involved, it did not become public knowledge until Stevenson reached the semifinals at [Wimbledon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Championships,_Wimbledon "The Championships, Wimbledon") in 1999, the first year she qualified to play in the tournament. Erving had provided financial support for Stevenson over the years, but had not otherwise been part of her life. The public disclosure of their relationship did not initially lead to contact between father and daughter; however, Stevenson contacted Erving in 2008 and they finally initiated a further relationship.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr_Jay#cite_note-espn-94) Erving met Stevenson for the first time on October 31, 2008.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr_Jay#cite_note-95) In 2009, Erving attended the [Family Circle Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Family_Circle_Cup "Family Circle Cup") tennis tournament to see Stevenson play, marking the first time he had attended one of her matches.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr_Jay#cite_note-96)

In 1988, Erving received the Golden Plate Award of the [American Academy of Achievement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_of_Achievement "Academy of Achievement").[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr_Jay#cite_note-97) In 2003, Erving fathered a second child outside of his marriage, Justin Kangas, with a woman named Dorýs Madden. Julius and Turquoise Erving were subsequently divorced and Erving continued his relationship with Madden, with whom he had three more children, Jules Erving and two others including Julieta who was born in 2005.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr_Jay#cite_note-espn-94) They married in 2008 and moved from [St. George, Utah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._George,_Utah "St. George, Utah") to [Buckhead, Atlanta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buckhead "Buckhead") in Georgia in 2009 while managing their Atlanta golf and country club.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr_Jay#cite_note-98)[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr_Jay#cite_note-99)

On September 10, 2021, Erving attended an unveiling ceremony at the University of Massachusetts Amherst for statues honoring himself and fellow UMass alumni and Basketball Hall of Fame members [John Calipari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Calipari "John Calipari"), [Marcus Camby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marcus_Camby "Marcus Camby") and [Jack Leaman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Leaman "Jack Leaman"). The ceremony was attended by former teammates, coaches, family and current players of the UMass men's and women's basketball teams.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr_Jay#cite_note-100)

**Ayoola Ogundeyi Jr.**[listen](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/transcoded/a/a3/Ayoola_Ogundeyi_Jr.wav/Ayoola_Ogundeyi_Jr.wav.mp3 "Play audio")[ⓘ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Ayoola_Ogundeyi_Jr.wav "File:Ayoola Ogundeyi Jr.wav") (born 9 August 1989),[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayo_Jay#cite_note-3) better known as **Ayo Jay**, is an English-born Nigerian singer. He currently has a record deal with One Nation and [RCA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RCA_Records "RCA Records"), and is also known as **Boy Wonder**.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayo_Jay#cite_note-4)

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ayo_Jay&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Ayo Jay discovered his abilities for singing and songwriting at a young age. After graduating from International School, [Lagos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagos "Lagos") (ISL) in 2006, Ayo Jay relocated to the United States to pursue a college degree in finance and investment from [Baruch College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baruch_College "Baruch College").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayo_Jay#cite_note-5)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ayo_Jay&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

In 2013, Ayo Jay signed a recording deal with One Nation Records and released "Your Number" on 21 June 2013.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayo_Jay#cite_note-6) The music video for "Your Number" was shot in Atlanta.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayo_Jay#cite_note-7) The song's remix features rap vocals by [Fetty Wap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fetty_Wap "Fetty Wap") and was released on 16 July 2015.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayo_Jay#cite_note-8) "Your Number" was re-released by [RCA Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RCA_Records "RCA Records") following Ayo Jay's record deal with the label.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayo_Jay#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayo_Jay#cite_note-10) On 28 February 2017, the song was certified gold by the [RIAA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recording_Industry_Association_of_America "Recording Industry Association of America").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayo_Jay#cite_note-11) On 23 August 2016, RCA Records released another remix, featuring [Chris Brown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Brown "Chris Brown") and [Kid Ink](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kid_Ink "Kid Ink").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayo_Jay#cite_note-12)

He currently has a record deal with One Nation and [RCA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RCA_Records "RCA Records"), and is also known as **Boy Wonder**.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayo_Jay#cite_note-4)

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ayo_Jay&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Ayo Jay discovered his abilities for singing and songwriting at a young age. After graduating from International School, [Lagos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagos "Lagos") (ISL) in 2006, Ayo Jay relocated to the United States to pursue a college degree in finance and investment from [Baruch College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baruch_College "Baruch College").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayo_Jay#cite_note-5)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ayo_Jay&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

In 2013, Ayo Jay signed a recording deal with One Nation Records and released "Your Number" on 21 June 2013.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayo_Jay#cite_note-6) The music video for "Your Number" was shot in Atlanta.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayo_Jay#cite_note-7) The song's remix features rap vocals by [Fetty Wap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fetty_Wap "Fetty Wap") and was released on 16 July 2015.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayo_Jay#cite_note-8) "Your Number" was re-released by [RCA Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RCA_Records "RCA Records") following Ayo Jay's record deal with the label.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayo_Jay#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayo_Jay#cite_note-10) On 28 February 2017, the song was certified gold by the [RIAA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recording_Industry_Association_of_America "Recording Industry Association of America").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayo_Jay#cite_note-11) On 23 August 2016, RCA Records released another remix, featuring [Chris Brown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Brown "Chris Brown") and [Kid Ink](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kid_Ink "Kid Ink").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayo_Jay#cite_note-12)

Musical artist

**Charles Nii Armah Mensah Jr.**, (born 17 October 1984) known by his [stage name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stage_name "Stage name")**Shatta Wale** ([pronunciation](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/transcoded/a/a6/Tw-Shatta_Wale.ogg/Tw-Shatta_Wale.ogg.mp3 "Play audio")[ⓘ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Tw-Shatta_Wale.ogg "File:Tw-Shatta Wale.ogg")), formerly **Bandana**,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-chattahse-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-2) is a [Ghanaian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghanaians "Ghanaians")[reggae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reggae "Reggae")-dancehall artist.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-3)

## Early life and education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shatta_Wale&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life and education")]

Charles Nii Armah Mensah Jr. was born in [Korle Gonno](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korle_Gonno "Korle Gonno") from [Accra, Ghana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Accra,_Ghana "Accra, Ghana") at the Police Hospital on 17 October 1984 to Charles Nii Armah Mensah Snr and Elsie Evelyn Avemegah. His father is a politician, businessman and legal practitioner.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-4)

He attended Seven Great Princes Academy at [Dansoman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dansoman "Dansoman"), a suburb in [Accra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Accra "Accra"), where he demonstrated an affinity for arts and acted in a popular drama series, _By the Fireside_, at the [National Theatre of Ghana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Theatre_of_Ghana "National Theatre of Ghana").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-5) He continued to the Winneba Secondary School, where he obtained his second cycle education.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-6)

At the start of his career, he was called Doggy.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-7)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shatta_Wale&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

Wale started with the stage name "Bandana" after senior high school, and released the hit track "Bandana from Ghana" in 2004.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-9)

Wale's 2004 recording "Moko Hoo" was nominated for a [Ghana Music Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghana_Music_Awards "Ghana Music Awards").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-10)

His sudden rise to fame happened at the 2013 VGMA awards, when he threw lyrical insults to the [VGMA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/VGMusic.com "VGMusic.com") (now Telecel Ghana Music Awards), because he said they had robbed him of the Dancehall Artist of the Year award. Although the song had vulgar lyrics, it was anticipated by the media, which created his musical breakthrough.

His biggest hit in 2013, "Dancehall King," gained significant radio airplay in Ghana.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-11) His primary source of revenue is hosting events, which attract thousands of young Ghanaians.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-12)

In 2014, he peaked at number 38 on [E.tv](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E.tv "E.tv")'s "Top 100 Most Influential Ghanaian" Awards chart.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-14) He has since then appeared on the chart every year.

In 2015, Wale asked not to be nominated in the [Vodafone Ghana Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vodafone_Ghana_Music_Awards "Vodafone Ghana Music Awards") even though he could have won the Artiste & Song of the year for the second time running with his hit songs "Dancehall Commando" featuring Sarkodie, "Party all night long" featuring [Jah Vinci](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jah_Vinci "Jah Vinci"), "Wine Ya Waist" featuring [Davido](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Davido "Davido"), and "Korle Gonno" among many hit songs he released the preceding year. Because of an impending court case with the organisers of the awards, Charter House Productions Ltd, for allegedly making defamatory remarks against the [CEO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chief_executive_officer "Chief executive officer") of Charter House in a video he uploaded on his [Facebook](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Facebook "Facebook") page.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-15)

His best-known singles are "Dancehall King", "My Level" and "Taking Over". "Dancehall King" earned him the Artiste of the Year at the 2014 edition of the [Vodafone Ghana Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vodafone_Ghana_Music_Awards "Vodafone Ghana Music Awards").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-16)

Wale is also an actor, and appeared in the films _Never Say Never,_[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-17)_The trial of Shatta Wale_[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-18) and _Shattered Lives_.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-19)

He was ranked "Most Influential Musician" on social media in 2017.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-20) He made a record-setting as a dancehall artist to have won 11 awards at the 2019 [3 Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/3_Music_Awards "3 Music Awards") ceremony.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-21)

## Concerts

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shatta_Wale&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Concerts")]

Wale was the first Ghanaian to organize a digital concert on [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube"), which was dubbed the Faith Concert. This was organized to bring hope to Ghanaians and his global audience at large during the fight against the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic").[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-28)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-29)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-30) He was selected by the Ministry of Communications, Ghana, alongside highlife musician [Kuami Eugene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kuami_Eugene "Kuami Eugene") as the headline artistes for the COVID-19 app virtual launch concert[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-31) held on Monday April 13, 2020.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-32)

On 31 December 2024, [Vybz Kartel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vybz_Kartel "Vybz Kartel") invited Wale to perform at his Freedom Street Concert in [Jamaica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamaica "Jamaica"), due to the love and support he had shown him over the years, even when Vybz Kartel was in prison. The show featured top international artistes like [Busta Rhymes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Busta_Rhymes "Busta Rhymes"), Chronic Law, Shawn Storm, Masicka, [Bounty Killer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bounty_Killer "Bounty Killer"), [Jah Vinci](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jah_Vinci "Jah Vinci"), [Rvssian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rvssian "Rvssian"), [Spice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spice "Spice"), and [Popcaan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Popcaan "Popcaan").[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-33)

On 18 October 2025, Wale hosted "Shatta Fest 2025 x Shattabration: The King Calls" at Black Star Square in Accra, drawing tens of thousands of fans for a free all-night concert. The event featured performances by top Ghanaian artists and tributes, marking his birthday celebration with support from MoMo Fest, Shaxi, and Charterhouse.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-34)

## Controversies

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shatta_Wale&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Controversies")]

In October 2021, Wale allegedly created a hoax that he was shot and was receiving treatment. He later turned himself in to the police.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-50) He was arrested by the [Ghana Police Service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghana_Police_Service "Ghana Police Service") for allegedly involved in the creation and circulation of information to create fear and panic.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-51)[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-52) He was remanded into prison custody for a week.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-53)[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-54)[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-55) On Tuesday, 26 October 2021, Shatta Wale was granted a GH¢100,000 self-recognizance bail at today's hearing. The case has been adjourned to November 9, 2021.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-56)[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-57)[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-58) A fortnight after the artist was released on bail, he got caught in another confrontation with the Police as he stormed out of meeting with celebrities called at the behest of Ghana's Police Chief. Shatta Wale complained of unfair treatment at the meeting after all his colleagues were allegedly allowed to use their phones and he was not. He later reported to the meeting, he is Currently in Jail in US.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-59)

In June 2025, Ghana's Economic and Organised Crime Office (EOCO) seized Wale’s 2019 Lamborghini Urus during a search at his Trassaco Valley residence. The operation followed a request from the U.S. [Federal Bureau of Investigation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Bureau_of_Investigation "Federal Bureau of Investigation") (FBI) in connection with Nana Kwabena Amuah, a Ghanaian convicted in the United States for money laundering and fraud.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-60)[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-61)

Wale voluntarily surrendered the car, but denied links to criminal activity, claiming he bought it for US $150,000 without knowledge of its alleged origins. He later accused EOCO's executive director of intimidation and abuse of power.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-62)[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-63)

EOCO described the operation as professional and identified Wale as a person of interest while awaiting a U.S. request to repatriate the vehicle under a mutual legal assistance treaty.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-64)

On 20 August 2025, Wale was detained after voluntarily appearing at the EOCO for questioning related to the Lamborghini, which U.S. authorities said may be linked to proceeds from a $4 million fraud case. He was held overnight and released the next day on bail. His bail conditions initially required GH₵10 million with two sureties, but these were later revised to GH₵5 million with continued obligations to report regularly to EOCO. Wale's legal team stated they were cooperating with authorities, and he remains a person of interest in the ongoing investigation.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-65)[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-66)[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-67)

## Feuds

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shatta_Wale&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Feuds")]

Being a controversial artiste in the Ghana music industry, Wale has had arguments with many of his fellow artistes, such as:

*   **Stonebwoy**:[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-68) In 2018, [Stonebwoy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stonebwoy "Stonebwoy") was asked about Shatta Wale's claim that Stonebwoy had refused to collaborate with him. Stonebwoy responded by saying that Shatta Wale had suggested that Stonebwoy was responsible for his mother's death in 2015. Shatta Wale denied the allegations in an interview. The beef escalated when Shatta Wale and his crew went up on stage to congratulate Stonebwoy after he won the Vodafone Ghana Music Awards for Dancehall Artiste of the Year. This led to Stonebwoy pulling out a gun on stage.
*   **Sarkodie**:[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-69) Shatta Wale has commented on his beef with [Sarkodie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarkodie_(rapper) "Sarkodie (rapper)"), saying that if he replies to Sarkodie, Sarkodie's mother will beg him to stop making music.

In 2023, Wale and Kwadwo Sheldon of Kwadwo Sheldon Studios (KSS) went into entertainment beefing. The source of this beef was a comment made by Sheldon: "In his songs, Shatta Wale portrays himself as a gangster, yet he contacted the police following an online dispute". Sheldon said in an interview that he was reported to the IGP of Ghana, [George Akuffo Dampare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Akuffo_Dampare "George Akuffo Dampare") by Wale on charges of belittling his work.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-70)[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-71) On May 3, 2024, upon Wale arriving at the London airport before his performance at Indigo at The O2, Wale visibly snubbed Sheldon, who had extended his hand in greeting.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-72)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shatta_Wale&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Wale has a son with Ghanaian socialite Michelle Diamonds. He proposed to Diamonds on stage at the launch of his _Reign_ album in 2018,[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-74) but they separated in 2019 over domestic violence issues.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-75)[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-76)

During an October 2023 interview with the BBC's Stefania Okereke, Shatta Wale expressed regret for not pursuing a career in law. He said he was considering becoming a lawyer in the future, when he feels "financially ready", despite his music career, as law was his initial aspiration.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-79)

Musical artist

**Charles Nii Armah Mensah Jr.**, (born 17 October 1984) known by his [stage name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stage_name "Stage name")**Shatta Wale** ([pronunciation](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/transcoded/a/a6/Tw-Shatta_Wale.ogg/Tw-Shatta_Wale.ogg.mp3 "Play audio")[ⓘ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Tw-Shatta_Wale.ogg "File:Tw-Shatta Wale.ogg")), formerly **Bandana**,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-chattahse-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-2) is a [Ghanaian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghanaians "Ghanaians")[reggae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reggae "Reggae")-dancehall artist.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-3)

## Early life and education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shatta_Wale&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life and education")]

Charles Nii Armah Mensah Jr. was born in [Korle Gonno](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korle_Gonno "Korle Gonno") from [Accra, Ghana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Accra,_Ghana "Accra, Ghana") at the Police Hospital on 17 October 1984 to Charles Nii Armah Mensah Snr and Elsie Evelyn Avemegah. His father is a politician, businessman and legal practitioner.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-4)

He attended Seven Great Princes Academy at [Dansoman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dansoman "Dansoman"), a suburb in [Accra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Accra "Accra"), where he demonstrated an affinity for arts and acted in a popular drama series, _By the Fireside_, at the [National Theatre of Ghana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Theatre_of_Ghana "National Theatre of Ghana").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-5) He continued to the Winneba Secondary School, where he obtained his second cycle education.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-6)

At the start of his career, he was called Doggy.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-7)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shatta_Wale&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

Wale started with the stage name "Bandana" after senior high school, and released the hit track "Bandana from Ghana" in 2004.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-9)

Wale's 2004 recording "Moko Hoo" was nominated for a [Ghana Music Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghana_Music_Awards "Ghana Music Awards").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-10)

His sudden rise to fame happened at the 2013 VGMA awards, when he threw lyrical insults to the [VGMA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/VGMusic.com "VGMusic.com") (now Telecel Ghana Music Awards), because he said they had robbed him of the Dancehall Artist of the Year award. Although the song had vulgar lyrics, it was anticipated by the media, which created his musical breakthrough.

His biggest hit in 2013, "Dancehall King," gained significant radio airplay in Ghana.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-11) His primary source of revenue is hosting events, which attract thousands of young Ghanaians.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-12)

In 2014, he peaked at number 38 on [E.tv](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E.tv "E.tv")'s "Top 100 Most Influential Ghanaian" Awards chart.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-14) He has since then appeared on the chart every year.

In 2015, Wale asked not to be nominated in the [Vodafone Ghana Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vodafone_Ghana_Music_Awards "Vodafone Ghana Music Awards") even though he could have won the Artiste & Song of the year for the second time running with his hit songs "Dancehall Commando" featuring Sarkodie, "Party all night long" featuring [Jah Vinci](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jah_Vinci "Jah Vinci"), "Wine Ya Waist" featuring [Davido](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Davido "Davido"), and "Korle Gonno" among many hit songs he released the preceding year. Because of an impending court case with the organisers of the awards, Charter House Productions Ltd, for allegedly making defamatory remarks against the [CEO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chief_executive_officer "Chief executive officer") of Charter House in a video he uploaded on his [Facebook](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Facebook "Facebook") page.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-15)

His best-known singles are "Dancehall King", "My Level" and "Taking Over". "Dancehall King" earned him the Artiste of the Year at the 2014 edition of the [Vodafone Ghana Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vodafone_Ghana_Music_Awards "Vodafone Ghana Music Awards").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-16)

Wale is also an actor, and appeared in the films _Never Say Never,_[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-17)_The trial of Shatta Wale_[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-18) and _Shattered Lives_.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-19)

He was ranked "Most Influential Musician" on social media in 2017.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-20) He made a record-setting as a dancehall artist to have won 11 awards at the 2019 [3 Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/3_Music_Awards "3 Music Awards") ceremony.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-21)

In 2019, Wale had a collaboration with Beyoncé titled "Already" on her album _[The Lion King: The Gift](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Lion\_King:\_The\_Gift "The Lion King: The Gift")_, which was nominated for a Grammy Award.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-23)

In 2021, he was nominated for two awards and won the 'Best Virtual Entertainer of the Year' Award at the International Reggae and World Music Awards (IRAWMA).[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-24)

Wale released a song in January 2024 titled "Balloon", with an accompanying video.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-25)

He performed at [Vybz Kartel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vybz_Kartel "Vybz Kartel")'s Freedom Street concert in [Jamaica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamaica "Jamaica").[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-26)

On April 10, 2025, Wale hosted Nigerian TikTok influencer [Peller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peller_(streamer) "Peller (streamer)") at his mansion in [Ghana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghana "Ghana"), sparking viral online attention through their collaborative videos and promotional appearances, particularly in connection with Shaxi, his ride-hailing company.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-27)

## Concerts

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shatta_Wale&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Concerts")]

Wale was the first Ghanaian to organize a digital concert on [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube"), which was dubbed the Faith Concert. This was organized to bring hope to Ghanaians and his global audience at large during the fight against the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic").[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-28)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-29)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-30) He was selected by the Ministry of Communications, Ghana, alongside highlife musician [Kuami Eugene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kuami_Eugene "Kuami Eugene") as the headline artistes for the COVID-19 app virtual launch concert[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-31) held on Monday April 13, 2020.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-32)

On 31 December 2024, [Vybz Kartel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vybz_Kartel "Vybz Kartel") invited Wale to perform at his Freedom Street Concert in [Jamaica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamaica "Jamaica"), due to the love and support he had shown him over the years, even when Vybz Kartel was in prison. The show featured top international artistes like [Busta Rhymes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Busta_Rhymes "Busta Rhymes"), Chronic Law, Shawn Storm, Masicka, [Bounty Killer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bounty_Killer "Bounty Killer"), [Jah Vinci](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jah_Vinci "Jah Vinci"), [Rvssian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rvssian "Rvssian"), [Spice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spice "Spice"), and [Popcaan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Popcaan "Popcaan").[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-33)

On 18 October 2025, Wale hosted "Shatta Fest 2025 x Shattabration: The King Calls" at Black Star Square in Accra, drawing tens of thousands of fans for a free all-night concert. The event featured performances by top Ghanaian artists and tributes, marking his birthday celebration with support from MoMo Fest, Shaxi, and Charterhouse.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-34)

## Awards and recognition

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shatta_Wale&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Awards and recognition")]

The [Mayor of Worcester](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mayor_of_Worcester,_Massachusetts "Mayor of Worcester, Massachusetts"), [Joseph Petty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joseph_Petty "Joseph Petty"), presented Wale with the [key to the city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Keys_to_the_City_in_the_United_States "List of Keys to the City in the United States") on 8 July 2017.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-35)

On 18 March 2018, Wale was presented an honoree award for his contribution to [reggae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reggae "Reggae") in Ghana at the 37th Annual [Chicago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago "Chicago") Music Awards (CMA), in conjunction with the 36th International Reggae & World Music Awards (IRAWMA).[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-36)

On 24 April 2025, Wale was recognized at the [University of Ghana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Ghana "University of Ghana")'s Brands and Marketing Masterclass, where his brand and marketing skills were studied.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-37)

Shatta Wale in 2026 has won many awards including Best African Dancehall Entertainer and Concert of the Year for his event, Shatta Fest at the 43rd IRAWMA.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-38)

## Endorsements

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shatta_Wale&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Endorsements")]

In 2014, Wale became a brand ambassador for [Guinness Ghana Breweries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guinness_Ghana_Breweries "Guinness Ghana Breweries").[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-39) and as the [brand ambassador](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brand_ambassador "Brand ambassador") for Rush Energy Drink.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-40)[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-41)[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-42)

In September 2017, [Kasapreko Company Limited](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kasapreko_Company_Limited "Kasapreko Company Limited"), producers of several alcoholic and non-alcoholic beverages in Ghana, unveiled Wale as their newest brand ambassador for Storm Energy Drink.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-43) 19 July 2023, Kasapreko Company Limited (KCL) renewed Wale's ambassador deal.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-44)

On 17 November 2017, Wale signed a deal with Boss Baker Beef Roll as the brand ambassador.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-45) Infinix Ghana, a smartphone company, on September 11, 2019, announced Shatta Wale as its brand ambassador.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-46)

## Philanthropy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shatta_Wale&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Philanthropy")]

On June 12, 2024, Wale supported the "Buzstop Boys" in a community clean up exercise at [Alajo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alajo "Alajo") in [Accra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Accra "Accra") and donated some amount through his foundation to the organization to keep up with their environmental initiatives.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-47)[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-48)

## Accra Invasion Project

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shatta_Wale&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Accra Invasion Project")]

On 16 September 2024, Wale announced the Accra Invasion Project (AIP), an initiative to discover and support talented individuals in [Accra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Accra "Accra"), the capital of Ghana. The project has since promoted nine artists: Papillon Blood, Shattonzy, Zicoranking, JoeQuaye, Blakid, Boy Cray, Kinjunia, Dosted Gennah, and Sanaa, the only female among them.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-49)

## Controversies

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shatta_Wale&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Controversies")]

In October 2021, Wale allegedly created a hoax that he was shot and was receiving treatment. He later turned himself in to the police.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-50) He was arrested by the [Ghana Police Service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghana_Police_Service "Ghana Police Service") for allegedly involved in the creation and circulation of information to create fear and panic.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-51)[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-52) He was remanded into prison custody for a week.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-53)[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-54)[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-55) On Tuesday, 26 October 2021, Shatta Wale was granted a GH¢100,000 self-recognizance bail at today's hearing. The case has been adjourned to November 9, 2021.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-56)[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-57)[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-58) A fortnight after the artist was released on bail, he got caught in another confrontation with the Police as he stormed out of meeting with celebrities called at the behest of Ghana's Police Chief. Shatta Wale complained of unfair treatment at the meeting after all his colleagues were allegedly allowed to use their phones and he was not. He later reported to the meeting, he is Currently in Jail in US.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-59)

In June 2025, Ghana's Economic and Organised Crime Office (EOCO) seized Wale’s 2019 Lamborghini Urus during a search at his Trassaco Valley residence. The operation followed a request from the U.S. [Federal Bureau of Investigation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Bureau_of_Investigation "Federal Bureau of Investigation") (FBI) in connection with Nana Kwabena Amuah, a Ghanaian convicted in the United States for money laundering and fraud.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-60)[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-61)

Wale voluntarily surrendered the car, but denied links to criminal activity, claiming he bought it for US $150,000 without knowledge of its alleged origins. He later accused EOCO's executive director of intimidation and abuse of power.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-62)[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-63)

EOCO described the operation as professional and identified Wale as a person of interest while awaiting a U.S. request to repatriate the vehicle under a mutual legal assistance treaty.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-64)

On 20 August 2025, Wale was detained after voluntarily appearing at the EOCO for questioning related to the Lamborghini, which U.S. authorities said may be linked to proceeds from a $4 million fraud case. He was held overnight and released the next day on bail. His bail conditions initially required GH₵10 million with two sureties, but these were later revised to GH₵5 million with continued obligations to report regularly to EOCO. Wale's legal team stated they were cooperating with authorities, and he remains a person of interest in the ongoing investigation.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-65)[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-66)[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-67)

## Feuds

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shatta_Wale&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Feuds")]

Being a controversial artiste in the Ghana music industry, Wale has had arguments with many of his fellow artistes, such as:

*   **Stonebwoy**:[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-68) In 2018, [Stonebwoy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stonebwoy "Stonebwoy") was asked about Shatta Wale's claim that Stonebwoy had refused to collaborate with him. Stonebwoy responded by saying that Shatta Wale had suggested that Stonebwoy was responsible for his mother's death in 2015. Shatta Wale denied the allegations in an interview. The beef escalated when Shatta Wale and his crew went up on stage to congratulate Stonebwoy after he won the Vodafone Ghana Music Awards for Dancehall Artiste of the Year. This led to Stonebwoy pulling out a gun on stage.
*   **Sarkodie**:[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-69) Shatta Wale has commented on his beef with [Sarkodie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarkodie_(rapper) "Sarkodie (rapper)"), saying that if he replies to Sarkodie, Sarkodie's mother will beg him to stop making music.

In 2023, Wale and Kwadwo Sheldon of Kwadwo Sheldon Studios (KSS) went into entertainment beefing. The source of this beef was a comment made by Sheldon: "In his songs, Shatta Wale portrays himself as a gangster, yet he contacted the police following an online dispute". Sheldon said in an interview that he was reported to the IGP of Ghana, [George Akuffo Dampare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Akuffo_Dampare "George Akuffo Dampare") by Wale on charges of belittling his work.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-70)[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-71) On May 3, 2024, upon Wale arriving at the London airport before his performance at Indigo at The O2, Wale visibly snubbed Sheldon, who had extended his hand in greeting.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-72)

## #OccupyJulorbiHouse

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shatta_Wale&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: #OccupyJulorbiHouse")]

Wale joined the discussion surrounding the OccupyJulorbiHouse protest, expressing his disapproval of the arrest of demonstrators who were marching towards [Jubilee House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jubilee_House "Jubilee House") on September 21. His criticism of the arrests garnered support from many of his fans, some of whom suggested that he should create a song dedicated to President Akufo-Addo.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-73)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shatta_Wale&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Wale has a son with Ghanaian socialite Michelle Diamonds. He proposed to Diamonds on stage at the launch of his _Reign_ album in 2018,[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-74) but they separated in 2019 over domestic violence issues.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-75)[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-76)

Wale and his girlfriend, Maali, announced the birth of their first child, a girl. They made their relationship public in 2023 after sharing photos and videos. This is Wale's fifth child but his first with Maali.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-77)[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-78)

During an October 2023 interview with the BBC's Stefania Okereke, Shatta Wale expressed regret for not pursuing a career in law. He said he was considering becoming a lawyer in the future, when he feels "financially ready", despite his music career, as law was his initial aspiration.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatta_Wale#cite_note-79)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

Nigerian singer (born 1991)

This article is about the Nigerian singer whose birth name is Oluwatosin Ajibade. For the Nigerian blogger, see [Tosin Ajibade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tosin_Ajibade "Tosin Ajibade").
