**Oluwatosin Oluwole Ajibade** ([listen](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/transcoded/0/02/Oluwatosin_Oluwole_Ajibade.wav/Oluwatosin_Oluwole_Ajibade.wav.mp3 "Play audio")[ⓘ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Oluwatosin_Oluwole_Ajibade.wav "File:Oluwatosin Oluwole Ajibade.wav"); born 19 July 1991),[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-1) better known by his stage name **Mr Eazi**, is a [Nigerian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nigerian "Nigerian") singer, songwriter, and record executive. He is the pioneer of Banku music, a fusion sound he describes as a mixture of [Ghanaian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghana "Ghana")[highlife](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Highlife "Highlife") and Nigerian chord progressions and patterns.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-Complex-2) Mr Eazi relocated to [Kumasi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kumasi "Kumasi") in 2008 and enrolled at [KNUST](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kwame_Nkrumah_University_of_Science_and_Technology "Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology"), where he began booking artists to perform at college parties. He showed interest in music after recording a guest verse on "My Life", a song that gained traction and became a popular record at KNUST. Mr Eazi released his debut mixtape, _About to Blow_, in 2013. He gained an international audience following the release of the [Efya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Efya "Efya")-assisted single "Skin Tight". His second mixtape, _Life Is Eazi, Vol. 1 – Accra to Lagos_, was released in 2017.

## Life and career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mr_Eazi&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Life and career")]

### Early life and education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mr_Eazi&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Early life and education")]

Oluwatosin Oluwole Ajibade was born in [Port Harcourt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_Harcourt "Port Harcourt"), the capital of [Rivers State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rivers_State "Rivers State").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-Noisey-4) He grew up in an entrepreneurial home and is a member of the [Yoruba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yoruba_people "Yoruba people") ethnic group. His mother was a business owner and his father owns a private aviation consulting practice.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-Noisey-4) While attending primary school in [Lagos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagos "Lagos"), Mr Eazi had a brief stint in the school's choir.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-Noisey-4) During his upbringing, he listened to songs his dad would play for the family while having breakfast.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-Highsnobiety-5) At age 16, Mr Eazi relocated to Ghana to further his educational endeavors, enrolling in the mechanical engineering program at [Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kwame_Nkrumah_University_of_Science_and_Technology "Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology") (KNUST).[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-Noisey-4) Mr Eazi started recording music during his time at the school, and contributed guest vocals to the track "My Life". The song gained traction and became a popular record at KNUST. Before that, he established a party and promotion company called Swagger Entertainment.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-Highsnobiety-5)

When he was 23 years old, he returned to Nigeria and opened an e-commerce platform.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-Noisey-4) In an interview with _[The Guardian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Guardian\_(Nigeria) "The Guardian (Nigeria)")_ newspaper, he said he briefly worked for [Schlumberger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schlumberger "Schlumberger") upon returning to Nigeria.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-The_Guardian_Life-6) He also said his business ventures included soft drinks import, [gold mining](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gold_mining "Gold mining"), and food distribution.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-The_Guardian_Life-6) Moreover, he told _Highsnobiety_ that he started about six business ventures.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-Highsnobiety-5) In 2014, Mr Eazi quit being a club promoter after an artist failed to show up for the largest party he attempted to throw.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-Highsnobiety-5)

### 2013–2015: _About to Blow_ and other releases

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mr_Eazi&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: 2013–2015: About to Blow and other releases")]

Mr Eazi released his 13-track debut mixtape, _About to Blow_, in July 2013.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-Jaguda1-7) It yielded the singles "Pipi Dance" and "Bankulize". The former was released in mid-2012, while the latter was released in 2013.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-Jaguda1-7) Mr Eazi recorded the mixtape with producer Klu and released it within a week.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-The_Fader_21-8)_[The Fader](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Fader "The Fader")_ magazine describes the mixtape as a "heavily dancehall-leaning SoundCloud playlist". Prior to releasing the mixtape, Mr Eazi worked with producers such as Magnom, Peeweezle, Nshona, Klumonsta, [D'Tunes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Tunes "D'Tunes"), and E-Kelly. Moreover, he was featured on Stay Jay's "Baby Lace" and Lousika's "Knockout".[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-Jaguda1-7) In 2014, Mr Eazi moved back to Nigeria and was contacted by British-Ghanaian producer [Juls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juls "Juls"), who got a hold of some of his recordings.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-Noisey-4) Due to not being able to locate the audio files of his old recordings, his attempt at working with Juls stalled for a long time.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-Noisey-4) He eventually retrieved his audio files and sent them to Juls, who made a new beat and created the artwork for the mixtape's second single "Bankulize".[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-Noisey-4) The song features vocals by Ghanaian hiplife artist [Pappy Kojo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pappy_Kojo "Pappy Kojo") and was released in November 2014.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-Noisey-4) The official remix of "Bankulize" features vocals by [Burna Boy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burna_Boy "Burna Boy") and was released in September 2016.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-9) Mr Eazi premiered the remix on [Ebro Darden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ebro_Darden "Ebro Darden")'s [Beats 1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beats_1 "Beats 1") radio show a month earlier.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-10)

In August 2015, Mr Eazi released the dancehall-influenced track "Skin Tight", which features vocals by [Efya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Efya "Efya") and was produced by DJ Juls.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-11) In an interview with _[Complex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Complex\_(magazine) "Complex (magazine)")_ magazine, Mr Eazi described the song as a "fusion".[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-Complex-2) He said he spoke Ghanaian pidgin on the delivery and used Nigerian melodies.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-Complex-2) In August 2016, Nigerian record producer [Cobhams Asuquo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cobhams_Asuquo "Cobhams Asuquo") released a rendition of the song. [DJ Caise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DJ_Caise "DJ Caise") released a house remix of the song in September 2016, while [Terry G](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terry_G "Terry G") collaborated with Mr Eazi to release a remix of the song.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-13) In April 2017, "Skin Tight" was featured in an ad for the vodka brand [Ciroc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ciroc "Ciroc").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-14)

Mr Eazi was featured on Eugy's 2016 hit single "Dance for Me". _[The Guardian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Guardian "The Guardian")_ newspaper included the song on its list of the 10 biggest African tracks of 2016.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-15) The music video for "Dance for Me" was directed by Vertex and Gabriella Kingsley.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-Clash-16) Robin Murray of _Clash_ magazine described the song as a "salute to their joint Ghanaian heritage".[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-Clash-16) On 17 June 2016, Mr Eazi released the R&B-inspired "Anointing", a song that features rap verses from Ghanaian rapper [Sarkodie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarkodie_(rapper) "Sarkodie (rapper)").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-17) He first announced plans for the song in May 2016.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-18)

### 2016–2017: GMA snub, Twitter backlash, _Accra to Lagos_, and record deal

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mr_Eazi&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: 2016–2017: GMA snub, Twitter backlash, Accra to Lagos, and record deal")]

In February 2016, organizers of the [Ghana Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghana_Music_Awards "Ghana Music Awards") made a decision not to nominate Mr Eazi in any of its Ghanaian-only categories.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-Pulse_Ghana-19) Charterhouse spokesperson George Quaye said Mr Eazi was disqualified because of his nationality and only eligible to compete in the African Artiste of the Year category.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-Pulse_Ghana-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-GhanaWeb-20) However, the singer failed to pick up a nomination in that particular category because the organizers felt he wasn't as big as the other nominees.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-GhanaWeb-20) On 11 January 2017, Mr Eazi tweeted that Ghanaian music has a great influence over present-day Nigerian music.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-21) He received heavy backlash after posting the tweet and trended nationwide in both Ghana and Nigeria. On 12 January 2017, Mr Eazi apologized to Nigerians for the comments he made.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-22)

Following his performance at the [2016 Ghana Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Ghana_Music_Awards "2016 Ghana Music Awards"), Wizkid announced that he signed Mr Eazi to his imprint Starboy Entertainment.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-23) However, the singer told Star FM Ghana that he is not officially signed to Starboy and is only in business with the imprint.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-24) Mr Eazi's second mixtape, _Life Is Eazi, Vol. 1 – Accra To Lagos_, was released on 10 February 2017.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-Pulse_11-25) The mixtape was initially scheduled for release on 11 February 2017, and debuted at number 4 on the _[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard\_(magazine) "Billboard (magazine)")_ World Albums chart.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-Pulse_11-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-26) The mixtape comprises 14 tracks, including three bonus tracks. Its production was handled by [Maleek Berry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maleek_Berry "Maleek Berry"), [Masterkraft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Masterkraft_(producer) "Masterkraft (producer)"), [Legendury Beatz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legendury_Beatz "Legendury Beatz"), and [Young John](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Young_John_(producer) "Young John (producer)"). Guest artists featured on the mixtape include [Tekno](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tekno_Miles "Tekno Miles"), [Olamide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olamide "Olamide"), [Phyno](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phyno "Phyno"), [Mugeez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mugeez "Mugeez"), [Medikal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medikal "Medikal"), [DJ Cuppy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DJ_Cuppy "DJ Cuppy"), [Falz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Falz "Falz"), and [Big Lean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_Lean "Big Lean").[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-27) Mr Eazi announced on Instagram that the mixtape sold 200,000 copies in pre-orders.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-28) While speaking to [Julie Adenuga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julie_Adenuga "Julie Adenuga") on her Beats 1 radio show, he said the mixtape is a tribute to the two cities that influenced the evolution of his sound.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-29)

The mixtape's lead single, "Leg Over", was produced by E-Kelly and released on 2 December 2016. The music video for "Leg Over" features cameo appearances from comedian [Eddie Kadi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eddie_Kadi "Eddie Kadi"), [Maleek Berry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maleek_Berry "Maleek Berry"), and Wizkid. Mr Eazi told Lawrence Burney from Noisey.com that the song is about being taken advantage of in a relationship.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-Noiseyy-30) He also said it was leaked and wasn't meant to be a single.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-Noiseyy-30) Upon its release in December 2016, "Leg Over" inspired numerous dance videos.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-31) Music in Africa's contributor Gabriel Myers Hansen described the song as "gentle and minimalist", and said it is "freshened by delicate string and percussion placements reminiscent of highlife from decades ago".[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-32) Mr Eazi released the mixtape's second single, "Tilapia", on 1 February 2017. It features a rap verse by Ghanaian rapper Medikal.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-33) On 1 March 2017, Mr Eazi released the [Sesan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sesan_Ogunro "Sesan Ogunro")-directed music video for "[In The Morning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In_The_Morning_(Mr_Eazi_song) "In The Morning (Mr Eazi song)")", which features vocals by Toronto rapper [Big Lean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_Lean "Big Lean").[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-34) On 1 April 2017, he released the Teekay-directed music video for "Fight", a song that features additional vocals from DJ Cuppy.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-35) On 7 April 2017, Mr Eazi released the music video for the Mugeez-assisted track "Business".[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-36)

### 2019-present: Coachella, Empawa Africa, and _The Evil Genius_

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mr_Eazi&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 2019-present: Coachella, Empawa Africa, and The Evil Genius")]

In January 2019, _Vanguard_ newspaper reported that Mr Eazi would perform at the 2019 [Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coachella_Valley_Music_and_Arts_Festival "Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival").[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-37) In August 2019, the singer launched emPawa Africa, a talent incubation initiative designed to nurture and support up-and-coming African artists. Thirty musicians were enrolled in the first edition and received grant and mentorship to scale up their music career. The initiative was supported by [YouTube Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube_Music "YouTube Music").[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-38)

Mr Eazi released his second Extended Play (EP), _Something Else_, on 19 February 2021.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-NewEP-39) On 10 June 2022, he released the single "[Legalize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legalize_(Mr_Eazi_song) "Legalize (Mr Eazi song)")" via his platform [emPawa Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EmPawa_Africa "EmPawa Africa"). Mr Eazi released his debut studio album, _[The Evil Genius](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Evil\_Genius\_(Mr\_Eazi\_album) "The Evil Genius (Mr Eazi album)")_, on 27 October 2023.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-40)

## Artistry

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mr_Eazi&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Artistry")]

Mr Eazi is known for pioneering [Banku music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afrobeats#Banku_music "Afrobeats"), a sound "characterized by percolating rhythms and laid-back vocal delivered in [Ghanaian Pidgin English](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghanaian_Pidgin_English "Ghanaian Pidgin English")".[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-Complex-2) His music largely fits into the category of [Afrobeats](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afrobeats "Afrobeats"), a contemporary West African pop genre that marries pop, [dancehall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dancehall "Dancehall"), [highlife](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Highlife "Highlife"), and [hip-hop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hip_hop_music "Hip hop music").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-Complex-2) Music critics have described his music as having an R&B-like quality reminiscent of artists such as [Beres Hammond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beres_Hammond "Beres Hammond") and [Gregory Isaacs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gregory_Isaacs "Gregory Isaacs").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-Noisey-4) Noisey's Lawrence Burney stated that Mr Eazi uses his deep voice to "give ballad-like qualities to dance-forward production".[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-Noisey-4)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mr_Eazi&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Mr Eazi is married to [Temi Otedola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Temi_Otedola "Temi Otedola"), daughter of Nigerian billionaire [Femi Otedola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Femi_Otedola "Femi Otedola") and sister to [DJ Cuppy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DJ_Cuppy "DJ Cuppy").[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-41) They got engaged on 10 April 2022 and married in 2025.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-42) A civil ceremony was held in [Monaco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monaco "Monaco") on 9 May, a traditional Yoruba wedding in [Dubai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dubai "Dubai") in July, and a church wedding in [Reykjavík](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reykjav%C3%ADk "Reykjavík").[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-43)[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-44)

Nigerian singer (born 1991)

This article is about the Nigerian singer whose birth name is Oluwatosin Ajibade. For the Nigerian blogger, see [Tosin Ajibade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tosin_Ajibade "Tosin Ajibade").

**Oluwatosin Oluwole Ajibade** ([listen](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/transcoded/0/02/Oluwatosin_Oluwole_Ajibade.wav/Oluwatosin_Oluwole_Ajibade.wav.mp3 "Play audio")[ⓘ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Oluwatosin_Oluwole_Ajibade.wav "File:Oluwatosin Oluwole Ajibade.wav"); born 19 July 1991),[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-1) better known by his stage name **Mr Eazi**, is a [Nigerian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nigerian "Nigerian") singer, songwriter, and record executive. He is the pioneer of Banku music, a fusion sound he describes as a mixture of [Ghanaian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghana "Ghana")[highlife](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Highlife "Highlife") and Nigerian chord progressions and patterns.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-Complex-2) Mr Eazi relocated to [Kumasi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kumasi "Kumasi") in 2008 and enrolled at [KNUST](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kwame_Nkrumah_University_of_Science_and_Technology "Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology"), where he began booking artists to perform at college parties. He showed interest in music after recording a guest verse on "My Life", a song that gained traction and became a popular record at KNUST. Mr Eazi released his debut mixtape, _About to Blow_, in 2013. He gained an international audience following the release of the [Efya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Efya "Efya")-assisted single "Skin Tight". His second mixtape, _Life Is Eazi, Vol. 1 – Accra to Lagos_, was released in 2017.

## Life and career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mr_Eazi&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Life and career")]

### Early life and education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mr_Eazi&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Early life and education")]

Oluwatosin Oluwole Ajibade was born in [Port Harcourt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_Harcourt "Port Harcourt"), the capital of [Rivers State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rivers_State "Rivers State").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-Noisey-4) He grew up in an entrepreneurial home and is a member of the [Yoruba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yoruba_people "Yoruba people") ethnic group. His mother was a business owner and his father owns a private aviation consulting practice.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-Noisey-4) While attending primary school in [Lagos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagos "Lagos"), Mr Eazi had a brief stint in the school's choir.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-Noisey-4) During his upbringing, he listened to songs his dad would play for the family while having breakfast.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-Highsnobiety-5) At age 16, Mr Eazi relocated to Ghana to further his educational endeavors, enrolling in the mechanical engineering program at [Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kwame_Nkrumah_University_of_Science_and_Technology "Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology") (KNUST).[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-Noisey-4) Mr Eazi started recording music during his time at the school, and contributed guest vocals to the track "My Life". The song gained traction and became a popular record at KNUST. Before that, he established a party and promotion company called Swagger Entertainment.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-Highsnobiety-5)

When he was 23 years old, he returned to Nigeria and opened an e-commerce platform.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-Noisey-4) In an interview with _[The Guardian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Guardian\_(Nigeria) "The Guardian (Nigeria)")_ newspaper, he said he briefly worked for [Schlumberger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schlumberger "Schlumberger") upon returning to Nigeria.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-The_Guardian_Life-6) He also said his business ventures included soft drinks import, [gold mining](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gold_mining "Gold mining"), and food distribution.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-The_Guardian_Life-6) Moreover, he told _Highsnobiety_ that he started about six business ventures.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-Highsnobiety-5) In 2014, Mr Eazi quit being a club promoter after an artist failed to show up for the largest party he attempted to throw.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-Highsnobiety-5)

### 2013–2015: _About to Blow_ and other releases

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mr_Eazi&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: 2013–2015: About to Blow and other releases")]

Mr Eazi released his 13-track debut mixtape, _About to Blow_, in July 2013.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-Jaguda1-7) It yielded the singles "Pipi Dance" and "Bankulize". The former was released in mid-2012, while the latter was released in 2013.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-Jaguda1-7) Mr Eazi recorded the mixtape with producer Klu and released it within a week.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-The_Fader_21-8)_[The Fader](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Fader "The Fader")_ magazine describes the mixtape as a "heavily dancehall-leaning SoundCloud playlist". Prior to releasing the mixtape, Mr Eazi worked with producers such as Magnom, Peeweezle, Nshona, Klumonsta, [D'Tunes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Tunes "D'Tunes"), and E-Kelly. Moreover, he was featured on Stay Jay's "Baby Lace" and Lousika's "Knockout".[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-Jaguda1-7) In 2014, Mr Eazi moved back to Nigeria and was contacted by British-Ghanaian producer [Juls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juls "Juls"), who got a hold of some of his recordings.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-Noisey-4) Due to not being able to locate the audio files of his old recordings, his attempt at working with Juls stalled for a long time.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-Noisey-4) He eventually retrieved his audio files and sent them to Juls, who made a new beat and created the artwork for the mixtape's second single "Bankulize".[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-Noisey-4) The song features vocals by Ghanaian hiplife artist [Pappy Kojo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pappy_Kojo "Pappy Kojo") and was released in November 2014.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-Noisey-4) The official remix of "Bankulize" features vocals by [Burna Boy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burna_Boy "Burna Boy") and was released in September 2016.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-9) Mr Eazi premiered the remix on [Ebro Darden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ebro_Darden "Ebro Darden")'s [Beats 1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beats_1 "Beats 1") radio show a month earlier.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-10)

In August 2015, Mr Eazi released the dancehall-influenced track "Skin Tight", which features vocals by [Efya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Efya "Efya") and was produced by DJ Juls.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-11) In an interview with _[Complex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Complex\_(magazine) "Complex (magazine)")_ magazine, Mr Eazi described the song as a "fusion".[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-Complex-2) He said he spoke Ghanaian pidgin on the delivery and used Nigerian melodies.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-Complex-2) In August 2016, Nigerian record producer [Cobhams Asuquo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cobhams_Asuquo "Cobhams Asuquo") released a rendition of the song. [DJ Caise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DJ_Caise "DJ Caise") released a house remix of the song in September 2016, while [Terry G](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terry_G "Terry G") collaborated with Mr Eazi to release a remix of the song.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-13) In April 2017, "Skin Tight" was featured in an ad for the vodka brand [Ciroc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ciroc "Ciroc").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-14)

Mr Eazi was featured on Eugy's 2016 hit single "Dance for Me". _[The Guardian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Guardian "The Guardian")_ newspaper included the song on its list of the 10 biggest African tracks of 2016.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-15) The music video for "Dance for Me" was directed by Vertex and Gabriella Kingsley.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-Clash-16) Robin Murray of _Clash_ magazine described the song as a "salute to their joint Ghanaian heritage".[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-Clash-16) On 17 June 2016, Mr Eazi released the R&B-inspired "Anointing", a song that features rap verses from Ghanaian rapper [Sarkodie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarkodie_(rapper) "Sarkodie (rapper)").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-17) He first announced plans for the song in May 2016.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-18)

### 2016–2017: GMA snub, Twitter backlash, _Accra to Lagos_, and record deal

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mr_Eazi&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: 2016–2017: GMA snub, Twitter backlash, Accra to Lagos, and record deal")]

In February 2016, organizers of the [Ghana Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghana_Music_Awards "Ghana Music Awards") made a decision not to nominate Mr Eazi in any of its Ghanaian-only categories.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-Pulse_Ghana-19) Charterhouse spokesperson George Quaye said Mr Eazi was disqualified because of his nationality and only eligible to compete in the African Artiste of the Year category.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-Pulse_Ghana-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-GhanaWeb-20) However, the singer failed to pick up a nomination in that particular category because the organizers felt he wasn't as big as the other nominees.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-GhanaWeb-20) On 11 January 2017, Mr Eazi tweeted that Ghanaian music has a great influence over present-day Nigerian music.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-21) He received heavy backlash after posting the tweet and trended nationwide in both Ghana and Nigeria. On 12 January 2017, Mr Eazi apologized to Nigerians for the comments he made.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-22)

Following his performance at the [2016 Ghana Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Ghana_Music_Awards "2016 Ghana Music Awards"), Wizkid announced that he signed Mr Eazi to his imprint Starboy Entertainment.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-23) However, the singer told Star FM Ghana that he is not officially signed to Starboy and is only in business with the imprint.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-24) Mr Eazi's second mixtape, _Life Is Eazi, Vol. 1 – Accra To Lagos_, was released on 10 February 2017.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-Pulse_11-25) The mixtape was initially scheduled for release on 11 February 2017, and debuted at number 4 on the _[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard\_(magazine) "Billboard (magazine)")_ World Albums chart.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-Pulse_11-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-26) The mixtape comprises 14 tracks, including three bonus tracks. Its production was handled by [Maleek Berry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maleek_Berry "Maleek Berry"), [Masterkraft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Masterkraft_(producer) "Masterkraft (producer)"), [Legendury Beatz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legendury_Beatz "Legendury Beatz"), and [Young John](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Young_John_(producer) "Young John (producer)"). Guest artists featured on the mixtape include [Tekno](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tekno_Miles "Tekno Miles"), [Olamide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olamide "Olamide"), [Phyno](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phyno "Phyno"), [Mugeez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mugeez "Mugeez"), [Medikal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medikal "Medikal"), [DJ Cuppy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DJ_Cuppy "DJ Cuppy"), [Falz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Falz "Falz"), and [Big Lean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_Lean "Big Lean").[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-27) Mr Eazi announced on Instagram that the mixtape sold 200,000 copies in pre-orders.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-28) While speaking to [Julie Adenuga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julie_Adenuga "Julie Adenuga") on her Beats 1 radio show, he said the mixtape is a tribute to the two cities that influenced the evolution of his sound.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-29)

The mixtape's lead single, "Leg Over", was produced by E-Kelly and released on 2 December 2016. The music video for "Leg Over" features cameo appearances from comedian [Eddie Kadi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eddie_Kadi "Eddie Kadi"), [Maleek Berry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maleek_Berry "Maleek Berry"), and Wizkid. Mr Eazi told Lawrence Burney from Noisey.com that the song is about being taken advantage of in a relationship.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-Noiseyy-30) He also said it was leaked and wasn't meant to be a single.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-Noiseyy-30) Upon its release in December 2016, "Leg Over" inspired numerous dance videos.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-31) Music in Africa's contributor Gabriel Myers Hansen described the song as "gentle and minimalist", and said it is "freshened by delicate string and percussion placements reminiscent of highlife from decades ago".[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-32) Mr Eazi released the mixtape's second single, "Tilapia", on 1 February 2017. It features a rap verse by Ghanaian rapper Medikal.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-33) On 1 March 2017, Mr Eazi released the [Sesan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sesan_Ogunro "Sesan Ogunro")-directed music video for "[In The Morning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In_The_Morning_(Mr_Eazi_song) "In The Morning (Mr Eazi song)")", which features vocals by Toronto rapper [Big Lean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_Lean "Big Lean").[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-34) On 1 April 2017, he released the Teekay-directed music video for "Fight", a song that features additional vocals from DJ Cuppy.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-35) On 7 April 2017, Mr Eazi released the music video for the Mugeez-assisted track "Business".[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-36)

### 2019-present: Coachella, Empawa Africa, and _The Evil Genius_

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mr_Eazi&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 2019-present: Coachella, Empawa Africa, and The Evil Genius")]

In January 2019, _Vanguard_ newspaper reported that Mr Eazi would perform at the 2019 [Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coachella_Valley_Music_and_Arts_Festival "Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival").[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-37) In August 2019, the singer launched emPawa Africa, a talent incubation initiative designed to nurture and support up-and-coming African artists. Thirty musicians were enrolled in the first edition and received grant and mentorship to scale up their music career. The initiative was supported by [YouTube Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube_Music "YouTube Music").[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-38)

Mr Eazi released his second Extended Play (EP), _Something Else_, on 19 February 2021.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-NewEP-39) On 10 June 2022, he released the single "[Legalize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legalize_(Mr_Eazi_song) "Legalize (Mr Eazi song)")" via his platform [emPawa Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EmPawa_Africa "EmPawa Africa"). Mr Eazi released his debut studio album, _[The Evil Genius](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Evil\_Genius\_(Mr\_Eazi\_album) "The Evil Genius (Mr Eazi album)")_, on 27 October 2023.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-40)

## Artistry

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mr_Eazi&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Artistry")]

Mr Eazi is known for pioneering [Banku music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afrobeats#Banku_music "Afrobeats"), a sound "characterized by percolating rhythms and laid-back vocal delivered in [Ghanaian Pidgin English](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghanaian_Pidgin_English "Ghanaian Pidgin English")".[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-Complex-2) His music largely fits into the category of [Afrobeats](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afrobeats "Afrobeats"), a contemporary West African pop genre that marries pop, [dancehall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dancehall "Dancehall"), [highlife](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Highlife "Highlife"), and [hip-hop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hip_hop_music "Hip hop music").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-Complex-2) Music critics have described his music as having an R&B-like quality reminiscent of artists such as [Beres Hammond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beres_Hammond "Beres Hammond") and [Gregory Isaacs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gregory_Isaacs "Gregory Isaacs").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-Noisey-4) Noisey's Lawrence Burney stated that Mr Eazi uses his deep voice to "give ballad-like qualities to dance-forward production".[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-Noisey-4)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mr_Eazi&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Mr Eazi is married to [Temi Otedola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Temi_Otedola "Temi Otedola"), daughter of Nigerian billionaire [Femi Otedola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Femi_Otedola "Femi Otedola") and sister to [DJ Cuppy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DJ_Cuppy "DJ Cuppy").[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-41) They got engaged on 10 April 2022 and married in 2025.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-42) A civil ceremony was held in [Monaco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monaco "Monaco") on 9 May, a traditional Yoruba wedding in [Dubai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dubai "Dubai") in July, and a church wedding in [Reykjavík](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reykjav%C3%ADk "Reykjavík").[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-43)[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr_Eazi#cite_note-44)

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ayo_Jay&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Ayo Jay discovered his abilities for singing and songwriting at a young age. After graduating from International School, [Lagos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagos "Lagos") (ISL) in 2006, Ayo Jay relocated to the United States to pursue a college degree in finance and investment from [Baruch College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baruch_College "Baruch College").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayo_Jay#cite_note-5)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ayo_Jay&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

In 2013, Ayo Jay signed a recording deal with One Nation Records and released "Your Number" on 21 June 2013.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayo_Jay#cite_note-6) The music video for "Your Number" was shot in Atlanta.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayo_Jay#cite_note-7) The song's remix features rap vocals by [Fetty Wap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fetty_Wap "Fetty Wap") and was released on 16 July 2015.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayo_Jay#cite_note-8) "Your Number" was re-released by [RCA Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RCA_Records "RCA Records") following Ayo Jay's record deal with the label.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayo_Jay#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayo_Jay#cite_note-10) On 28 February 2017, the song was certified gold by the [RIAA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recording_Industry_Association_of_America "Recording Industry Association of America").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayo_Jay#cite_note-11) On 23 August 2016, RCA Records released another remix, featuring [Chris Brown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Brown "Chris Brown") and [Kid Ink](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kid_Ink "Kid Ink").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayo_Jay#cite_note-12)
